SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - DECEMBER 2, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to approve or ratify travel expenses for City-related business or to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

Closed Session Report
If the City Council adjourns to Closed Session, the City Council will reconvene into Open Session after its conclusion and designated City staff will provide a verbal report on any reportable action taken. This report will be memorialized in the official meeting minutes.
13.
Adjournment

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY, DECEMBER 2, 2024,
7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

 1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Ryan Klement, New Life Community Church.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by the Pat Nixon Musical Troupe.

 4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce W. Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

 5.  Presentations/Appointments

 5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council honoring:

  Dr. Nitin Shah (Recognition of humanitarian efforts and outstanding medical career).

 5B.  Informational update on the Tuesday, March 4, 2024 General Municipal Election.

  An informational update on the Tuesday, March 4, 2024 General Municipal Election was
  given by Cynthia Nava, Acting City Clerk. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no further action on this item.

  Mayor Solanki announced the meeting rules of decorum.

 6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Cynthia Nava, Acting City Clerk, announced that prior to the meeting the
  Council/Agency members received full-text, unredacted copies of the one (1) written
  comment submitted for Item 6, by the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in
  the official record. Requests for copies of the written comments submitted for this
  meeting can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Mel Cortez requested public notification of Santa’s Holiday Float winners and float
  riders.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Case Van der Linden requested recently planted parkway magnolia trees be replaced
  with trumpet trees.

  Sam Desai requested the public comment time at City public meetings be restored to a
  five (5) minute limit and spoke regarding City strategic planning priorities and resident
  participation in the strategic planning process.

  Bani Mukherji requested continued stronger collaboration between the City and
  residents.

  Anil Ramineni requested the addition of more pickleball courts in the City.

  Devang Adharyu expressed concern regarding large groups playing soccer and
  consuming alcoholic beverages on Sundays at Frontier Park, and requested information
  on where to report if unpermitted teams and illegal activities occur.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7B.2. Approval of Fiscal Year 2024-25 budget amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Johnson, to authorize administrative
  initiated Fiscal Year 2024-25 budget amendments in accordance with Joint Budget
  Resolution No. 2024-12/CSA No. 2024-01 and the Strategic Financial Plan and Budget
  Preparation Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  Account/Project: 110-451-61020 (Animal Control Services)
  Amount:  $429,351
  Justification: A budget amendment is requested to reallocate funds from the General
  Fund to cover outstanding invoices for Animal Control Services from Fiscal Year 2023-
  24. Although sufficient budget was allocated for these services during Fiscal Year 2023-
  24, the invoices for the last three quarters of the fiscal year, totaling $429,351, were
  not received until November 8, 2024. As the unspent allocation was returned to the
  General Fund at the close of Fiscal Year 2023-24, this amendment is necessary to
  ensure payment of the outstanding invoices (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki

7C.  Continuance of the existence of a local emergency concerning a gasoline leak from a
  privately-owned existing pipeline on the Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine public golf course, and
  potential threat to the safety of persons and property requiring remediation, repair, and
  improvement of the public golf course and other City-owned public property, as
  specified (COUNCIL).

  This item was pulled from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration by Mayor Pro
  Tem Vo.

  An explanation of the local emergency was given by Robert A. Lopez, City Manager.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Johnson, to:

  1. Continue the local emergency as proclaimed in Resolution No. 2023-05, at the
  Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine Golf Course and the nearby City property containing the C-
  4 well site;

  2. Make the findings set forth in Sections one (1) through eight (8) of Resolution No.
  2023-05, and incorporate by reference those findings, as they relate to the
  continued existence of a local emergency as specified; and

  3. Direct staff to provide a report to the City Council regarding the local emergency at
  least once every sixty (60) days, pursuant to Section 8630(c) of the California
  Government Code, until the City Council terminates the local emergency (COUNCIL).

7E.  Waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS ADOPTING THE CERRITOS ELECTRIC UTILITY RENEWABLE ENERGY

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZING UTILIZATION OF RESTRICTED COMMUNITY

  BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS, TOTALING APPROXIMATELY $181,000, DURING

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration by the City Council of the City of Cerritos of measures the City
  has taken to reduce crime, and review and consideration of additional measures that
  could be utilized to support crime reduction efforts, including consideration of the
  feasibility of creating a standalone City Police Department (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager and Cerritos Sheriff’s
  Station Captain Dru Strong. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to take actions to broadcast future
  Community Safety Committee (CSC) Meetings and relocate the CSC regular meeting
  location to the Council Chamber.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Mel Cortez thanked the City for recent increased public safety measures and inquired
  whether fumigation alarms could still be checked out from the Community Safety
  Services Division.

  Arti Adhvaryu expressed concern regarding the wait time to deliver public comment on
  this Item and reported a burglary instance in her neighborhood and inquired how to
  respond to an instance when witnessing a suspicious vehicle without license plates.

  Jignesh Mehta expressed concern regarding a recent attempted burglary at a local
  pharmacy and thanked the City for increased public safety measures and the prevention
  of the burglary at this facility.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, December 2, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 7 of 10

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  Anil Ramineni thanked the City for increased public safety measures and inquired
  regarding the potential use of bicycles for security patrol and expressed concern
  regarding the lack of lit homes in the evenings in the neighborhoods, providing
  suggestions for improvements. He also requested more scheduled Community Safety
  Committee meetings.

  Unidentified speaker thanked the City for increased public safety measures and inquired
  regarding the implementation of Proposition 36; and inquired regarding the additional
  placement of gated communities in the City.

  Amit Desai thanked the City for increased public safety measures and requested the
  City Council not authorize an additional funding allocation for a rebate program for
  residents who purchase new security cameras and/or home alarm systems, but use the
  funding instead toward additional increased City public safety measures.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to authorize Fiscal Year 2024-
  25 budget amendments for, and direct staff to schedule an agenda report for City
  Council review and consideration of award of any necessary contracts, at the next
  scheduled City Council meeting, if feasible, to proceed with implementation of the
  additional crime abatement options presented in the agenda report associated with this
  item, as follows:

  1. Authorize funding up to $140,400 to contract with a Southwest Patrol or another
  private security company, to provide three (3) unarmed private security guards
  to conduct high visibility patrols in residential neighborhoods eight hours per
  day, five days per week, in accordance with the City’s Purchasing and
  Contracting Policy;

  2. Authorize funding up to $44,500 to hire an additional part-time Cerritos
  Community Services Officer (CSO) to provide high visibility patrols in
  neighborhoods, respond to service calls involving property crime, gather
  fingerprint/DNA evidence, provide traffic control as directed, and issue parking
  citations;

  3. Authorize funding up to $40,000 for the law enforcement special operations
  fund, annually. This funding will be used to pay for overtime shifts for deputies
  engaged in dedicated crime suppression patrols;

  4. Authorize funding in the amount of $68,000 for the purchase of an additional
  CSO patrol vehicle equipped with a hazard light bar, Los Angeles Sheriff’s
  Department (LASD) mobile digital computer, and LASD radio;

  5. Authorize funding in the amount of $40,000 for a cost-sharing rebate program
  for residents who purchase new security cameras and/or a home alarm system,
  up to $200 per household, for a maximum of 200 households; and

  6. Direct staff to schedule on a future agenda, a report for City Council review and
  consideration of potential amendments to the Cerritos Municipal Code, to update
  fines levied by the City for false alarm calls made to the Cerritos Sheriff’s Station
  (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  Monday, December 2, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 8 of 10

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS PROVIDING FOR

  FOR FULL-TIME NON-EXEMPT EMPLOYEES REPRESENTED BY THE AMERICAN
